title: Neural-ODE for pharmacokinetics modeling and its advantage to alternative machine learning models in predicting new dosing regimens

content.abstract_summary: First application of neural-ODE to pharmacokinetics modeling, using clinical PK data from trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1, HER2+ breast cancer mAb-drug conjugate). Compares neural-ODE, lightGBM, LSTM, and NLME (two-compartment nonlinear mixed-effects) on 675 patients from two dosing regimens (Q3W n=647, Q1W n=28). Cross-regimen validation — training on Q3W, predicting Q1W — is the key evaluation. Neural-ODE substantially outperforms all alternatives on cross-regimen generalization; all models perform similarly within-regimen. Genentech (Lu J), published in iScience 2021.
key_findings: First study to apply neural-ODE to PK modeling — establishes neural-ODE as the foundational architecture for all subsequent neural ODE pharmacometrics work
Cross-regimen validation: neural-ODE RMSE 10.61 / R² 0.76 / Pearson 0.89 vs lightGBM RMSE 18.50 / R² 0.27, LSTM RMSE 19.56 / R² 0.15, NLME RMSE 15.21 / R² 0.68 — all bootstrap p < 0.05
Within-regimen validation: all models similar — neural-ODE RMSE 13.50 / R² 0.88; NLME 18.64 / 0.79 (only significant difference). Key message: neural-ODE advantage is extrapolation not interpolation

Neural-ODE correctly predicts PK falling to zero when dosing stops; LSTM and lightGBM predict nonzero values — LSTM learns from TIME not explicit dosing; neural-ODE directly incorporates dosing into state via ODE integration
Data augmentation (time-series truncation at 1008/1512/2016 hr) was required to prevent overfitting — real-world datasets are too small without augmentation; Q1W has only 28 patients
Architecture: GRU encoder → 12-element latent (6 mean + 6 std, variational) → ODE solver (4-layer FC, 16 hidden) → decoder. ODE directly incorporates dose events; code at zenodo + GitHub
limitations: Single drug (T-DM1, conjugated mAb) — generalizability to small molecules, different PK structures (e.g., flip-flop, enterohepatic recirculation) not demonstrated
Q1W cohort very small (n=28) — cross-regimen test set is underpowered for robust performance comparison
No mechanistic hybrid: the neural ODE replaces the entire ODE RHS rather than augmenting a known compartmental structure — identifiability and parameter interpretability not addressed
Individual-level only (not population NLME): IIV and between-subject variability not modeled by neural-ODE in this paper
Data augmentation required — implies NODEs cannot be trained on sparse clinical data without model-based simulation pre-training

extracted_claims.text: To date, neural-ODE is the most accurate PK model in predicting untested treatment regimens.

The advantage of the neural-ODE model may come from its ability to deal with unevenly sampled data points. The alternative deep learning models such as LSTM tend to assume even sampling. Neural-ODE directly incorporates dosing and timing data into the model at the decoder stage.

numerical_findings.description: Total T-DM1 patients (Q3W: 647, Q1W: 28, total: 675); records: 16,472
Cross-regimen RMSE: neural-ODE vs lightGBM vs LSTM vs NLME
Cross-regimen R²: neural-ODE vs lightGBM vs LSTM vs NLME

gaps_addressed: The foundational benchmark for M1.1 — any WG review of neural ODE PK must cite this as the origin. Establishes the key evaluation criterion: cross-regimen generalization (not held-out patients from same protocol)

The LSTM/lightGBM dosing-stop failure is a concrete pedagogical example of why the ODE structure matters — directly usable in the WG scoping paper's argument for mechanistic-constrained architectures over pure deep learning
